learningObjective: Precisely define the scale and zero-point of an affine quantizer and the dequantization formula.

canonicalClaims.claim: Affine quantization maps real x to integer q via q = round(x / s) + z, with dequantization x_hat = (q - z) * s. Scale s > 0 is the step size and zero-point z is the integer representing real zero.
conditions: Standard ONNX / PyTorch / TensorRT affine convention.
nonImplications: Does not imply symmetric quantization (z=0) is always preferred.
Does not include the clamp-to-integer-range step, which is separate.

misconceptions.claim: Quantization uses q = round(x * s) + z (multiplication by scale).
misconceptions.whyWrong: Larger s means larger step size, so we divide x by s to convert to integer steps.

misconceptions.claim: Zero-point z is a real-valued offset applied after scaling.
misconceptions.whyWrong: z is an integer (same dtype as q); it identifies which integer represents real zero.

misconceptions.claim: Symmetric quantization is just asymmetric quantization with z rounded to nearest integer.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Symmetric quantization enforces z = 0 by construction; it is not an approximation of asymmetric.

misconceptions.claim: The dequantization formula is x_hat = q * s (no zero-point subtraction) even for asymmetric quantization.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Asymmetric quantization requires subtracting z before scaling; otherwise the zero of the integer range is not the zero of the real range.

implementationFacts: In symmetric quantization, z = 0 and the formula simplifies to q = round(x / s), x_hat = q * s.
In INT8 asymmetric per-tensor, z lies in [0, 255] (unsigned) or [-128, 127] (signed).
performanceScenarios: Asymmetric quantization allows post-ReLU activations (natural zero-point at 0) to map efficiently.
